judge: Opus 5.5 (fresh adversarial reviewer agent, no prior scores)
rubric: height vs cliff, edge seams, style vs beodeul cliffs, front-elevation look, 1x readability

majors: Front-elevation look: the cut face is a near-uniform vertical panel (flat mid-tan fill with horizontal dash marks that read as masonry courses) with a dark shadow band along its bottom rows, exactly like a cliff base. Nothing reads as a surface sloping up and away; in the village crops (terra32/33, sol31 @(3,10), sol32 @(4,10)) it looks like a recessed wall niche/door in the cliff, not a ramp.

Edge seam: hard horizontal value step at the boundary between the face rows and the foot cell (last 16 rows) - the face ends on a dark shadow row and the foot starts on lighter flat dirt, so a continuous slope is visibly broken into 'wall + floor' across the full width.
minors: Side cheeks are straight full-height columns (dark brown left, flat orange right) not present on native beodeul cliffs; they read as wooden posts framing the cut.
Foot cell is a clean rectangle with straight edges and a slightly greyer/flat tint; in probe-3x it is wider than the ragged dirt road below and shows hard corners against grass.
Face texture is lower-contrast, finer noise than the chunky clustered cobbles of the native cliff face; looks washed out next to it.
1x readability weak: at 1x (probe-1x) the ramp is a faded patch in the cliff band; only the road continuity tells you it is passable.

majors: Top tread (top ~4-5 rows of the face) is overlaid with scattered green and near-white speckle noise, so at 1x/3x (probe-1x leftmost stairs, probe2 right stacked lower flight) the whole h1 cut reads as a grassy/frosted fringe or broken rubble, not as two clean steps.
Style inconsistency within the set: h1 stone is lighter and noisier (single-pixel white flecks) than the clean dressed treads of h2-h4, so the same paved road changes material at one-level cliffs.
minors: Side cheeks are full-height straight columns (dark brown left, flat orange right) not present on native cliffs; the orange right strip reads as a wooden plank.
Foot cell cobble has no light kerb edge, while the paved road tile above/below does; small visible break at the foot.
Treads are drawn as front-elevation stone courses with only a 1px light lip; acceptable stair read but tread depth is minimal.

majors: Right stack in probe2 (1 + strip + 2): the lower stairs flight is stairs-h1 and reads as a white/green speckled fringe, so the composed flight looks broken at the bottom.

Ramp stacks (probe2 middle and right, terra32/33 crossings) compose two flat wall-like panels with a dark shadow row and hard face/foot seam each; the composition reads as two niches separated by a ledge, not one continuous climb.
minors: Stairs 2+strip+2 stack joins cleanly at the landing (foot cobble lies on the strip and meets the next flight's crest); this part is fine.
Ramp foot cell on the landing strip is a flat rectangle wider than the dirt path.

summary: Heights match the native cliff rows in every probe and village crop (no wrong-height defect found). All 8 ramps fail: the cut face is a flat vertical panel with a cliff-style dark base shadow and a hard value step into the foot cell, so it reads as a niche/wall in the cliff, not a slope. Stairs h2-h4 read clearly as stairs and pass with minors (posts-like side cheeks, kerbless foot). Stairs h1 (both widths) fail: the top tread is covered in green/white speckle noise and reads as a grassy fringe at 1x. Stacked art fails because it inherits these defects; the stairs 2+2 stack itself joins cleanly. Side note (not graded as piece art): the two 'south cliff 2' ramp crossings in sol31 @(14,32) and sol32 @(20,32) show no cliff or ramp at all in the crop.
